Either there is no such remote computer or it refuses every connection. When that computer does run the NI-VISA server, the server could be an incompatible release or could be listening on some other port.

Access to the resource was refused because the user or machine in use lacks the required privileges, the instrument rejected the credentials VISA presented, or the credential information does not correspond to valid credentials.

The DAQmx function that waits for the next sample clock found that at least three clock ticks were missed since it was last called, so the program is falling behind the clock and some data was lost before the application could read it. Use a slower sample clock, or restructure the application so DAQmx Read runs more frequently. Turning on the property Convert Error to Warning does not help, because the data has already been lost.

The DAQmx function that waits for the next sample clock found that one or more clock ticks were missed since it was last called, so the program is falling behind the clock. Use a slower sample clock or change the application so it keeps pace; alternatively, turn on the property Convert Errors to Warnings and handle the resulting warning.
DAQmx Write had not finished when the next sample clock arrived, so the program is falling behind the hardware clock. Use a slower hardware clock or change the application so it keeps pace.

DAQmx Read had not finished when the next change detection event or sample clock arrived, so the program is falling behind the external change event or the hardware clock. With sample clock timing, use a slower hardware clock or make the application keep pace; with change detection timing, make the events less frequent or make the application keep pace.
DAQmx Write received no samples with which to initialize the buffered generation.
Either buffering is off for this task or it contains no channels. Without a buffer, call the scalar variant of the function; without channels, give the task at least one.
A sample clock timebase divisor cannot be set while the sample clock source is external. Either use the onboard clock as the sample clock source or leave the timebase divisor unconfigured.

The device is not accessible. It may have been removed from the system, be unpowered or have briefly lost power, have had its device or chassis driver support uninstalled, or be damaged. Check that it is connected and switched on, that the current driver version supports the device and chassis, and its status in NI MAX, then restart the computer; if damage is suspected, contact National Instruments support at ni.com/support.
Your hardware lacks support for DAQmx Signal Events, the group made up of Counter Output, Sample Complete, Sample Clock and Digital Change Detection events.

The onboard memory of the device underflowed: system or bus bandwidth limits kept the driver from writing data to the device as fast as the device was outputting it. Lower the sample rate, switch from interrupts to DMA or USB Bulk if interrupts are used, or run fewer programs at the same time.
A buffer that small prevents generation from starting; choose a bigger buffer size.
A buffer that small prevents acquisition from starting; choose a bigger buffer size.
A required parameter received a NULL pointer.

NI-DAQmx cannot create virtual channel names for certain physical channels, since the number appended to those names would become too large. Give each physical channel an explicit virtual channel name, or use a smaller trailing number for the final group of virtual channel names.
For input operations, the Prescaled Values must not contain the same number more than once.

The operation could not be carried out because the digital lines are reserved or NI-DAQmx does not see the device, possibly because another task holds the lines or a device reset is in progress. If another task uses the lines, wait for it to finish, or reset the device to force that task to release them; if a reset is under way, wait until it completes.
The analog data being written is above or below the allowed range. Adjust the Minimum Value and the Maximum Value so they match the channel range.

Self-calibration did not succeed and the self-calibration date was left unchanged. Disconnect external signals from the device, since they can add noise, and perform an external calibration so the onboard reference voltage used by self-calibration gets recalibrated.
The write failed because the data contains a different number of channels than the task. Provide data for every channel in the task, or change the task so its channel count matches the data.

The EEPROM calibration constants that correct the cal ADC readings are not valid, either because a calibration was done incorrectly or because the EEPROM data is corrupted. Calibrate the device externally, or get in touch with National Instruments Technical Support.
The channel cannot be added because the task already contains a channel with that name.
This operation is not allowed while the task is in the running state.
This operation is not allowed because the task contains no devices.

The generation cannot start because nothing has been written to the output buffer; a buffered generation needs data written to it first. Resizing the buffer, unreserving the task, a change to the Regeneration Mode property, modifying the Sample Mode, or setting up retriggering all empty the buffer.
The device does not support this property, or the property does not apply to this task.
An invalid value was wired to Task/Channels In; this control has to identify either a valid task or one or more valid virtual channels.
The sample clock source that was requested is not valid.

The strain gage calibration failed. Check that strain gages are attached to every specified strain channel, that their wiring suits the bridge type configuration, that the location given for the shunt resistor is correct, and that any hardware jumpers are set properly.
No custom scale exists under the requested name.
NI-DAQmx cannot communicate with the device. Check that the device is in the system, accessible, and not in the middle of a reset.

Not all of the requested samples have been acquired yet. To wait for them, read later or increase the read timeout; to get them sooner, raise the sample rate. If the task has a start trigger, check its configuration; if the task is set up for external timing, make sure an external clock is actually supplied.
The application is falling behind the hardware acquisition. A larger buffer, more frequent reads, or reading a set number of samples rather than all available samples may fix this.
The buffer cannot hold the samples that were requested to be written.
The identifier given for the device is not valid.
With Programmed IO selected as the Data Transfer Mechanism, the buffer size has to be zero. Either make the buffer size zero or choose a Data Transfer Mechanism other than Programmed IO.
This device has no such physical channel. Check the device documentation for the channels it provides.

With a computer name, confirm that it is valid, try pinging it and check that a DNS server is configured correctly. With TCP Open Connection, neither the remote port nor the service name may be 0.
